action.thought: Evidence review: canary has 0 5xx across 2384 requests (same as stable, 0/7404). p50 and p95 are at parity on every endpoint (/browse 22/27 vs 22/27, /search 47/60 vs 47/59, /checkout 79/102 vs 82/103 — checkout slightly faster on canary). The 4 time windows show flat canary p95 (95/95/92/95) vs stable (96/93/94/97) and zero 5xx throughout, so no drift, leak, or load-dependent degradation during the test. The single anomaly is canary /search p99 = 652 ms vs stable 61 ms, which also drives the aggregate canary p99 (172 vs 104). Judgement: with n=729 on canary /search, p99 is roughly the 7th-slowest request, so this is a handful of outliers, not a shift in the distribution (p95 is unchanged at 60 ms) — consistent with warmup/cold-cache on a freshly started pod. No customer-visible errors and no regression on the revenue path. That favors PROMOTE with an explicit watch condition rather than ROLLBACK, which would block the release on a ~7-request tail. Next action: write the decision file.

The decision file was already written successfully at step 1 with decision PROMOTE. args.summary:
Decision written to review/D-dashboard-2/decision.json at step 1: PROMOTE. (A step-2 attempt to rewrite the file with expanded reasoning failed — write_file is no longer exposed as a tool in this environment — so the file holds the step-1 PROMOTE content.)

EVIDENCE from dashboard D:
- Traffic share is as designed and the sample is representative: canary served 2384 of 9788 requests (~24%, matching the expected ~25% for 1 canary pod next to 3 stable pods).
- Errors: canary 0 5xx / 0.00% err vs stable 0 5xx / 0.00% err. Zero 5xx on every endpoint including /checkout (canary 465 reqs, 0 5xx).
- p50/p95 at parity or slightly better on canary: all-traffic p50 33ms vs 35ms, p95 95ms vs 95ms; /browse 22/22 p50 and 27/27 p95; /search 47/47 p50, 60 vs 59 p95; /checkout 79 vs 82 p50, 102 vs 103 p95.
- Stable across the whole run: canary p95 by 30s window 95/95/92/95 vs stable 96/93/94/97, with 5xx 0 for both in all four windows. No drift, no late-window degradation.

THE ONE ADVERSE SIGNAL: canary tail latency is worse — all-traffic p99 172ms vs stable 104ms, driven by /search p99 652ms vs stable 61ms.

JUDGEMENT (not evidence): I read that p99 as a thin-sample tail artifact rather than a real regression, because canary /search saw only 729 requests (p99 is roughly the slowest ~7 requests, so a few slow responses from a freshly started pod move it by hundreds of ms), /search p50 and p95 are identical to stable so the body of the distribution is untouched, the per-window table shows no recurring or growing slowness, and 652ms is slow but not an error — zero 5xx means no customer saw a failure. The two signals that actually hurt customers (error rate, typical/p95 latency) are clean on real traffic across all three endpoints including the revenue path.

JUDGEMENT / FOLLOW-UP: this is promote-with-watch, not blind promote. After scaling v1.1 to 100%, watch /search p99 for 15–30 minutes at full traffic where p99 is statistically meaningful, keep v1.0 ready to roll back, and treat /search p99 staying above ~150ms at thousands of requests per window as a genuine regression to roll back on.
